answer: Each new identity must lock a refundable bond in escrow and solve a proof-of-work puzzle seeded by the epoch, so a forger pays compute plus capital for every extra account, scaling linearly. Peers verify a signed cipher of the bond receipt and echo the result across the network. Honest agents register once, so the one-time cost is trivial, and a ridge in the reward curve favors long-lived identities over throwaway ones.
